title: 3.3.14 Plain English to Pseudocode: Looping Over an Array
description: Turn plain-English steps into pseudocode for a loop over an array with a check inside it: start the counter, look at each price, add one when it is under 10, and print once at the end.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR

  B --> C{{i = 0 to prices.length - 1}}
  C -- next item --> D{is the price under 10?}

  E --> C

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Start `cheapCount` at `0`.

**2.** Go through every price in the `prices` array, one at a time.

**3.** For each price, check whether it is under `10`. If it is, add one to `cheapCount`.

**4.** After the loop has finished, print `cheapCount` once.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor (open the Flow Chart bar). You do not draw it, you read it: the hexagon is the loop, the diamond sits inside it, and the print leaves from the hexagon's "done" exit.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Number every line, including indented ones. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET lives TO 3` (start a value)
- `IF lives is 0` ... `END IF` (a check, with the steps inside it indented)
- `FOR EACH life IN lives` ... `END FOR` (repeat for every item)
- `PRINT lives` (show something)

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.

Before you submit, trace it by hand with the real array `4.50, 12.00, 7.25, 30.00, 2.00`. Follow your own steps and count. If you do not land on **3**, something is in the wrong place even if Grade is green.
hints: The check is inside the loop, and the adding is inside the check: only a cheap price adds one.
The print is after the loop ends (after END FOR), once, not inside it.

requirements.title: Numbered steps
requirements.description: Number your steps 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: Write at least four lines that start with a number, each with a step written after it.

requirements.hint: Add a loop step that goes through each price in the prices array.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your steps
aiCheck.prompt: The student was given plain-English steps and rewrote them as numbered, step-by-step pseudocode in README.md, between a first line and a last line that were already there. The program is: const prices = [4.50, 12.00, 7.25, 30.00, 2.00]; let cheapCount = 0; for (let i = 0; i < prices.length; i++) { if (prices[i] < 10) { cheapCount = cheapCount + 1; } } console.log("Items under $10:", cheapCount). The point is a decision nested inside a loop: a price that is not cheap still moves on to the next one, and the print happens once, after the loop. Judge each criterion ONLY by whether its idea is present in the student's steps, however they word it. Plain English, keywords such as SET, IF, ELSE, END IF, FOR EACH, END FOR, CALL, PRINT, or a mix of both are all fine, and so are different names, different capitalisation, and different ways to number the lines. Do not require any particular keyword. A step that is clearly aimed at the criterion is enough for 'met'. Mark a criterion 'missing' only when the idea is absent or the steps do the opposite (for example the print inside the loop, or the counter set to 0 inside the loop). Write each note for THIS student's own steps: in a not-met note, name the exact step or word in their steps that causes the problem (quote at most a few words), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected steps. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their steps satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: Numbered steps
rubric.description: The student numbered their steps (1. 2. 3. or similar), at least four of them.

rubric.title: cheapCount starts at 0
rubric.description: cheapCount (or an equivalent counter) is set to 0 BEFORE the loop starts. Setting it to 0 inside the loop, or not at all, is missing.

rubric.title: A loop over the prices
rubric.description: The steps repeat for every price in the prices array (FOR EACH, a counted loop, "go through each", or similar).

rubric.title: Each price is checked against 10
rubric.description: A check asks whether a price is under 10 (price < 10 or equivalent). A different number or the opposite direction is missing.

rubric.title: A cheap price adds one
rubric.description: Adding ONE to the counter happens inside that check, so only a cheap price counts. Adding the price itself, adding outside the check, or adding every time is missing.

rubric.title: The print comes after the loop
rubric.description: The count is printed once AFTER the loop ends, not inside the loop.
